reads.sell: A lean, steely Chardonnay from the cool north of Burgundy, green apple and lemon over a chalky, oyster shell edge. Bright and dry with no new oak, it wants oysters or a simply grilled sole.

why.grape: No loud aroma of its own: the wine reads as chalk, lees and a soft cream from malolactic on a medium frame, the shape shifting Chardonnay seen without new oak.
why.climate: Tart green apple and lemon, acidity at medium plus or high and moderate alcohol say a cool continental site.

reads.sell: A fuller white Burgundy from the Côte de Beaune, yellow apple and peach wrapped in cream, hazelnut and a little toast from new oak. Dry, structured and long, it is a wine for roast chicken, lobster or a butter sauce.

why.grape: Butter and cream from malolactic, hazelnut from lees and toasty new oak around a stony core point to Chardonnay in the Burgundian cellar style.
why.climate: Ripe but restrained yellow fruit, acidity still near medium plus and alcohol short of high read as the warmer end of a cool continental climate, never the tropical ripeness of a warm one.

reads.sell: A sunny, rounded white Burgundy from the Mâconnais, ripe peach and yellow apple with a creamy texture and a gentle frame of new oak. Generous and dry, it suits roast chicken, pork or a creamy mushroom dish.

why.grape: Cream from malolactic and a light frame of vanilla and toast on a dry white with no aromatic signature of its own read as Chardonnay, rounder and less stony than the Côte de Beaune.
why.climate: Riper peach and yellow apple with acidity still at medium or medium plus place it at the warm southern end of Burgundy's cool continental climate.

reads.region: Napa Valley, Sonoma County and Central Coast
reads.sell: A rich, sun ripened California Chardonnay, pineapple, peach and baked apple folded into butter, vanilla and toast. Full bodied and dry, it stands up to lobster, crab cakes or roast chicken in a cream sauce.

why.grape: Lavish butter from malolactic, vanilla and toast from new oak and lees on a full body, with no aromatic grape signature, is Chardonnay dressed by the cellar.
why.climate: Stone and tropical fruit at full ripeness and alcohol at medium plus or high, yet acidity held at medium or medium plus, read as a moderate climate: strong sun to ripen, Pacific fog and San Pablo Bay breezes to keep the acid.
